I think most of the love for Boba Fett comes from the sense of mystery that gets built around his character. We learn very little about him, but the few things we can glean from the original trilogy (mostly Empire) paint him as a serious threat.

The first villain we meet in Star Wars is Darth Vader -- a towering man/machine whose first action is to lift a rebel soldier into the air and choke him with a single hand. Later we see an Imperial officer badmouth Vader and promptly get force-choked. Darth Vader is powerful and has a short temper. These things are confirmed and built upon by his actions in The Empire Strikes Back.

When Vader calls on a variety of bounty hunters to help him find the Millennium Falcon, he only directly speaks to one of them: Boba Fett. And what does he say? "No disintegrations." Evidently Boba Fett is known for completely disintegrating his targets and has to be told by Vader to tone it down and take them alive. Boba Fett responds to the most dangerous person in the room with a cool, emotionless "As you wish."

Boba Fett proceeds to outsmart Han Solo (probably the cleverest character we've met) and track him to Cloud City. It hardly matters that he doesn't directly capture them -- all he had to do was find them and allow Imperial forces to take them captive. Why do more work than you have to?

Once Vader arrives at Cloud City we see more dialogue between the two. The interesting part about their scenes together is how comfortable Boba acts around Vader. He isn't afraid to speak up and remind him that Han Solo is "No good to me dead," and Darth Vader acknowledges his concerns and promises compensation in the event of Han's death. This may seem trivial, but recall how intimidated everyone else seems to be when dealing with Vader.

We rarely see Boba Fett in action, but his attitude speaks volumes. Combine that with a 100% awesome suit of armor and a rockin' ship, and you have a fan favorite.

Now, about Return of the Jedi... This movie is was a real let down in terms of Boba Fett. We got all that build up in The Empire Strikes Back but end up getting very little payoff. There are a couple cool moments, but in the end Fett just ends up looking comically inept -- I won't argue with you there. It starts off good, though. We see Boba react to Leia's thermal detonator in a different way than the rest of Jabba's rabble. He immediately aims his weapon at her, and later gives her a nod of respect, almost as if he would have used a similar tactic. Once on the sail barge, Boba doesn't hesitate to engage Luke (using his awesome jetpack in the process), even though the latter is wielding a lightsaber (which Boba presumably recognizes as a jedi weapon). There was a lot of potential, I think, for a show down between Skywalker & company and Boba Fett, but instead we see him die in a way that completely contradicts what we thought we knew about him.

Oh, and since you mentioned Clone Wars...everything in that movie was terrible, Boba/Jango included. It was just an attempt to ape off the popularity of the character and sell more action figures. Hopefully we never have to see Disney make Boba Fett spinoff movie and completely ruin any sense of mystery that the character still has.

Btw I'm not a rabid Boba Fett fan, I just think he's kinda cool. I didn't really mean to go on for this long, but you made me think about why I actually like him, so kudos for that.

TL; DR - He's mysterious, looks cool, and nothing seems to faze him. Shame about ROTJ though.
